label: Relatives who could be tested
title: Telling relatives who could be tested
intro: Relatives may want to know their own status. You can tell them about testing without sharing your result.
steps: Keep it about health, never about blame.
Share where to get tested, not your own result.
If you prefer, send an anonymous notice through GeneBridge.
phrases: A condition may run in our family. Testing is free and confidential.
Being a carrier is common and doesn't mean you're ill.
You can find out privately. Nobody else needs to know.

drafts.detail: A condition may run in our family. Being a carrier is common: most carriers are completely healthy and never know it. It mainly matters when planning children. A simple blood test can show your own status. It's free and confidential, and you decide who, if anyone, sees the result.
